newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore gas oil seen strong despite bearish news.
newsitem.headline: Singapore gas oil seen strong despite bearish news.

text.p: Singapore gas oil (diesel) prices remained resilient despite several bearish news leading traders to expect firmer prices in the near future.
"Market sentiments are turning bullish as prices have not fallen despite the low India award and build up of stocks in South Korea," one trader said on Wednesday.
State-owned Indian Oil Corp (IOC) purchased a record low of 120,000 tonnes of high speed diesel for October delivery which caught the market by surprise but prices were unmoved.
Some traders said the market has already factored in the lower import volume by lowering prices several cents on Friday before the tender was awarded.
Trading sources said support was seen for physical gas oil at around $25.30 per barrel free-on-board (fob) Singapore basis ($188.50 per tonne) for exports to China and Indonesia.
Indonesia raised its September purchases to about 3.5 million barrels due to the scheduled maintenance of a 200,000-barrel-per-day (bpd) crude distillation unit at Cilacap next month.
Demand has also emerged from China. Chinese buyers were willing to buy gas oil at about $200 per tonne c-and-f southern China basis, with freight costs estimated at about $10 per tonne, traders said.
Industry sources said South Korea had sold about three spot cargoes in recent days to both traders and Chinese endusers.
The recent exports had reduced September availabilties from South Korea to about three-to-four cargoes from the previous seven to 10 cargoes, traders said.
One source said prices were also boosted by prompt purchases by a Singapore-based trader who paid a hefty 68-cent premium to Singapore spot prices for a 30,000-tonnes cargo.

The market was also bullish because the east-west spread is at a low $2.00 per tonne. The differential between Singapore gas oil prices over London had in the past rose to over $15 per tonne, traders said.
As a result, should gas oil prices in the west fall, there is a greater chance that prices in Singapore will not be affected, they added.
September paper gas oil paper which traded down to a low of $25.35 per barrel on Friday and was traded earlier this week around $25.55. Paper for September is currently quoted at $25.50-25.60.
